note: A qualifications bill that only names the Access to Information Act as governing access to its database; it states nothing on the Act's standing, rules or application.

facts.fact: The Star reports that Kenya enacted the Access to Information Act, 2016, giving effect to Article 35 of the Constitution, and that a forum assessed its implementation by public institutions.
The Star reports that the 2023 Access to Information Regulations, made under the Act, define proactive disclosure and set what public entities must publish.

facts.fact: The Daily Nation reports that the Access to Information Act guarantees the right to information under Article 35 of the Constitution; the document gives no year for it, so the date is the article's publication date.

note: The amendment bill is a classification and state secrets bill (class other), so it gives no draft fact.

facts.fact: The Commission on Administrative Justice (Ombudsman) says it will engage 54 public institutions to strengthen compliance with the Access to Information (ATI) Act, 2016, and says many institutions do not routinely publish information the Act requires.

note: The 813 complaints are administrative-justice complaints, not stated to be requests under the ATI Act; no figure for ATI requests.

facts.fact: The document is the text of Kenya's Access to Information Act, 2016, which gives effect to Article 35 of the Constitution, sets out a right to information and how to apply to public entities, and confers oversight and enforcement on the Commission on Administrative Justice; the text carries no assent or commencement date, so the year is the Act's.
Pollicy says Kenya's Access to Information Act of 2016 sets the process for requesting and handling information applications.
UNESCO states Kenya has enacted the Access to Information Act (2016), with a constitutional guarantee under Article 35.
UNESCO reports that the Commission on Administrative Justice, with a commissioner in charge of access to information, has reported uneven compliance among public institutions.

note: The ruling rests on constitutional Articles 35 and 47 and names no access to information law or decision on a request under it.

facts.fact: The Commission on Administrative Justice reports it issued orders under section 23(2)(a) of Kenya's Access to Information Act 2016, so the Act is in operation.

The Commission on Administrative Justice says it ordered the Kenya Institute of Management's CEO on 16 June 2025 to release records requested under the Act, and the applicant confirmed receipt on 24 June 2025.

note: Statement is on AI imagery and privacy; says nothing on an access to information law.
